articles.title: The WMO Says This Could Be the Strongest El Niño on Record. India's Food Supply Is in the Path.
articles.excerpt: An 80 per cent probability of El Niño by August, 90 per cent through November, and sea surface temperatures 6°C above average. The monsoon is already late.
articles.image_caption: Cracked earth in a drought-hit region — the WMO warns 2026 could bring the strongest El Niño ever recorded
articles.nri_angle: El Niño threatens higher food prices in India, potential rice and wheat export bans that affect diaspora food imports, and a harder macroeconomic environment that complicates the RBI's rate decisions — all directly impacting remittance value and NRI family budgets back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Added 172,000 Jobs. A Fed Rate Hike Is Now the Base Case. Here Is What That Means for NRIs.
articles.excerpt: May payrolls crushed forecasts, the unemployment rate held at 4.3 per cent, and the probability of a December rate hike jumped to 70 per cent. The dollar-rupee equation just shifted.
articles.image_caption: The US Federal Reserve building in Washington — markets now see a 70 per cent chance of a rate hike by December
articles.nri_angle: A Fed rate hike strengthens the dollar and pressures the rupee, directly affecting remittance values. Strong job growth supports H-1B sponsorship but the sectors hiring fastest are not tech — while long-term unemployment is rising among younger, educated workers who overlap with H-1B and OPT visa holders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The FAO Says Global Cereal Output Will Shrink for the First Time in Years. Two Crises Are Converging.
articles.excerpt: Wheat prices are up for a fourth straight month, fertiliser costs are spiking from the Hormuz closure, and the strongest El Niño on record is forming. The impact on Indian kitchens is coming.
articles.image_caption: A wheat field at harvest time — global cereal production is forecast to shrink 2 per cent in 2026-27
articles.nri_angle: Food inflation in India directly erodes the purchasing power of remittances. A weak monsoon plus global cereal tightening could push staple prices higher, hitting NRI families who support relatives back home. Potential export bans on rice and wheat would also affect diaspora communities who import Indian staples.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Economy Grew 7.8% Last Quarter. The Hard Part Starts Now.
articles.excerpt: Farm output and construction drove a surprise beat over forecasts, but the Iran war, a weak rupee and a subpar monsoon threaten to drag growth below 7% this year.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street, the symbolic heart of India's financial markets

sources.label: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Oman Just Zeroed Out Tariffs on 98% of Trade. Gulf NRIs Stand to Gain the Most.
articles.excerpt: The India-Oman CEPA came into force on June 1, opening duty-free access across textiles, seafood, gems and 127 services sub-sectors. For the 700,000 Indians in Oman, the agreement reshapes everything from job markets to business opportunities.
articles.image_caption: The Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque in Muscat, a landmark in the Omani capital where India-Oman trade ties are deepening
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Senate Just Voted $70 Billion for Deportations. Indians in America Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: The bill funds ICE and Border Patrol for three years, expands detention capacity, and arrives as the Indian government pushes back against the handcuffing of deportees on U.S. flights.
articles.image_caption: The floor of the United States Senate, where the $70 billion immigration enforcement bill was passed in a 52-47 vote
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Just Made It Cheaper for NRIs to Park Dollars in India. Here Is What Changed.
articles.excerpt: India's central bank will cover the full hedging cost for banks raising diaspora deposits, raise NRI equity investment limits, and scrap capital gains tax on foreign-held government bonds — a package analysts say could pull in $40 billion.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, where policymakers unveiled measures targeting diaspora deposits
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's New Grid Rules Could Cut Wind Farm Revenue by 48 Percent. A Court Just Hit Pause.
articles.excerpt: Tougher penalties for solar and wind producers who miss delivery targets have alarmed investors and forced a legal standoff — just as India needs billions to reach its 500 GW clean energy goal.
articles.image_caption: A solar power installation in India, where new grid rules threaten to slash developer revenues
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Says a Trade Deal With India Is Coming. The US Ambassador Says It Is 99% Done.
articles.excerpt: Three days of face-to-face talks in New Delhi wrapped up on June 4. Both sides say only technical legal language remains before the interim pact can be signed.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump speaks to reporters in the Oval Office
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Delhi Hotel Fire Killed 21 People. Seventeen Were Foreign Nationals Who Came for Medical Care.
articles.excerpt: Flourish Stay B&B in Malviya Nagar had one staircase, sealed windows, and no fire protection. Victims came from Liberia, Nigeria, Mozambique, and Bangladesh.
articles.image_caption: Firefighters battling a building fire during rescue operations
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Signed Nine Trade Deals in Three Years. Six More Are Coming.
articles.excerpt: The India-Oman CEPA went live on June 1, the US deal is 99% done, and Commerce Ministry officials say three to four more agreements will be executed in the next twelve months.
articles.image_caption: A commercial port handling trade cargo
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Launched Its First Flex-Fuel Car. Five Thousand Ethanol Pumps Will Follow by 2027.
articles.excerpt: Maruti Suzuki's WagonR now runs on 100 percent ethanol. The government plans 500 stations this year and 5,000 by December 2027 to cut a $120 billion fuel import bill.
articles.image_caption: Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri, who announced India's flex-fuel station rollout alongside Prime Minister Modi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US and Iran Are One Signature Away From Reopening the Strait of Hormuz. India Cannot Afford a Collapse.
articles.excerpt: Negotiators have agreed on terms that would extend the ceasefire by 60 days and unblock the world's most important oil chokepoint. Trump has not yet signed.
articles.image_caption: Satellite image of the Strait of Hormuz, the maritime chokepoint at the center of US-Iran ceasefire talks
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Used the Shangri-La Dialogue to Talk to Everyone. That Was the Point.
articles.excerpt: In Singapore, Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh held meetings with US INDOPACOM, NATO's military chief, the Swedish defence ministry, the Netherlands, and Singapore's president — all in 48 hours. India's message: strategic autonomy is not isolation.
articles.image_caption: The Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore, Asia's premier defence summit
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Wants India to Go Nuclear. This Time, the Private Sector Is Leading.
articles.excerpt: US Ambassador Sergio Gor says Washington and New Delhi are pushing civil nuclear cooperation to 'new levels' — with private companies, not governments, building the reactors India needs to power its AI ambitions.
articles.image_caption: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor, who is pushing for a private sector-led civil nuclear partnership with India
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nine Hundred Tankers Went Dark to Cross the Strait of Hormuz. India Is One of the Countries Paying for Passage.
articles.excerpt: Two-thirds of outbound oil tankers are switching off tracking systems to slip through Iran's blockade. Some are paying Tehran up to $2 million per crossing — and India, China, Pakistan, and Japan are among those using the corridor.
articles.image_caption: Oil tankers near the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for a fifth of global oil supply
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Canada Just Launched a Trade Forum. The Real Prize Is a Free Trade Deal by December.
articles.excerpt: Piyush Goyal and Mark Carney are fast-tracking CEPA negotiations that could unlock a $50 billion trade corridor and reshape economic ties for 2.8 million Indian-Canadians.
articles.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal led the trade delegation to Canada
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Man Tore the Indian Flag Outside a Texas City Hall. The Video Went Global in Hours.
articles.excerpt: The Frisco incident comes as anti-Indian sentiment intensifies in North Dallas, where the Indian-origin population has tripled since 2010. Community leaders say the debate has crossed a line.
articles.image_caption: Houston City Hall illuminated at night. Photo: Pexels
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Almost Missed the World Cup. Then Zee Signed an Eight-Year Deal Ten Days Before Kickoff.
articles.excerpt: Zee Entertainment secures FIFA broadcast rights through 2034 for roughly $60 million, ending months of uncertainty and launching the Unite8 Sports network in the process.
articles.image_caption: The FIFA World Cup trophy displayed at a tournament event
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Held Rates. Then It Threw the Rupee a Lifeline India's Bond Market Has Never Seen.
articles.excerpt: Capital gains tax scrapped for foreign bond investors, NRI deposit schemes sweetened, and concessional forex swaps extended — all in a single policy announcement aimed at stopping the rupee's slide.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee currency notes and coins reflecting the central bank rate decision
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is About to Pay Companies to Process Lithium and Nickel. The Minimum Entry Is 30,000 Tonnes.
articles.excerpt: A ₹3,000 crore incentive package for critical mineral processing is imminent, targeting the chokehold China has on India's EV battery supply chain.
articles.image_caption: Electric vehicle battery cells on a manufacturing line
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Subhash C Kashyap, the Man Who Defined How India's Parliament Works, Is Dead at 97
articles.excerpt: The former Lok Sabha Secretary-General authored over 100 books on constitutional law and served Parliament for nearly four decades, from Nehru's first Lok Sabha to the ninth.
articles.image_caption: Subhash C Kashyap, former Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tim Cook's Final Keynote Is on Monday. Apple Is Betting Everything on AI It Can Run on Your Phone.
articles.excerpt: WWDC 2026 will unveil a Siri overhaul powered by Google's Gemini, an edge-AI strategy that prioritises on-device processing, and a bill-splitting feature in Apple Wallet. It is also the last major stage for the CEO who turned Apple into a $3 trillion company.
articles.image_caption: Tim Cook, Apple CEO, at a public appearance in March 2026
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Drone Just Hit Oman's Largest Oil Terminal. India's Hormuz Bypass Is No Longer Safe.
articles.excerpt: The explosion at Mina al Fahal extends the Middle East conflict beyond the Strait of Hormuz and into the open-ocean infrastructure India was counting on to keep crude flowing.
articles.image_caption: Cargo ships docked near oil storage tanks at a coastal port facility
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Reliance's Hiring Has Slowed to a Crawl. AI Is About to Make It Worse.
articles.excerpt: India's largest private employer grew headcount by just 4% last year, one quarter of the previous year's pace. At TCS and Infosys, the workforce has already shrunk. The AI squeeze is only beginning.
articles.image_caption: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani at a company event in Mumbai
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: PhysicsWallah Killed Its Lending Plan One Week After Announcing It. The Stock Surged 18%.
articles.excerpt: The edtech giant scrapped a ₹120 crore student lending bet after investors revolted — and the market rewarded the U-turn instantly.
articles.image_caption: PhysicsWallah co-founder Alakh Pandey built the edtech platform from a YouTube channel
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New York's State Senate Just Declared August 15 India Independence Day. The Man Behind It Was Adopted From Kolkata.
articles.excerpt: Resolution J1935 urges Governor Kathy Hochul to formally recognise India's 79th Independence Day across the state — sponsored by the first Asian American elected to state office from upstate New York.
articles.image_caption: The New York State Senate adopted Resolution J1935 recognising India Independence Day
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Buying Oil From Venezuela, Brazil, Angola and Nigeria. The Hormuz Shutdown Forced Its Hand.
articles.excerpt: As the Strait of Hormuz enters its fourth month of near-total closure, Indian refiners have quietly built a new supply chain stretching from Latin America to West Africa — a structural shift that may outlast the conflict.
articles.image_caption: A crude oil tanker at sea — India's refiners are now sourcing from Latin America and Africa to offset Hormuz losses
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A New Bill Wants to Kill the H-1B Lottery and End OPT. Indian Tech Workers Are in the Crosshairs.
articles.excerpt: Republican Chip Roy's American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act would replace the visa lottery with a wage-based system, ban companies that laid off workers from hiring H-1B holders, and abolish the OPT program that hundreds of thousands of Indian students rely on.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Representative Chip Roy of Texas, who introduced the American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian Court Just Ruled That ChatGPT Is Not an Intermediary. It Is a Creator.
articles.excerpt: The Calcutta High Court's classification of generative AI as an 'originator' under the IT Act strips it of safe-harbour protection and opens a legal frontier India has no framework to govern.
articles.image_caption: The Calcutta High Court, where Justice Ravi Krishan Kapur issued the landmark AI classification ruling
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The OECD Just Gave the World One Month to Reopen the Strait of Hormuz. India Cannot Afford to Wait.
articles.excerpt: Global growth could fall to levels not seen since the 2008 crisis if Gulf energy supplies remain cut off. Asian economies, including India, are in the direct line of fire.
articles.image_caption: OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann at a press conference
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Monsoon Just Arrived Three Days Late. The Forecast Behind It Is the Worst India Has Seen in 11 Years.
articles.excerpt: IMD puts the chance of a deficient monsoon at 60 percent as El Niño strengthens, colliding with an oil shock and a weakening rupee to create the tightest squeeze Indian farmers have faced this decade.
articles.image_caption: Monsoon rains are the lifeblood of India's agricultural economy, delivering nearly 70 percent of annual rainfall
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Sent a Market Economist to the World Bank. That Has Never Happened Before.
articles.excerpt: Neelkanth Mishra — IIT gold medalist, Credit Suisse veteran, Aadhaar chairman, PM adviser — replaces Parameswaran Iyer in a three-year appointment that signals a shift from bureaucrats to strategists in India's multilateral representation.
articles.image_caption: The World Bank headquarters in Washington, DC, where Mishra will serve a three-year tenure
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Venezuela's Acting President Flew to Delhi With an Oil Deal India Could Not Refuse.
articles.excerpt: Delcy Rodríguez's visit cements Venezuela as India's fourth-largest crude supplier, with talks extending into mining, pharma, and critical minerals as the Hormuz crisis reshapes global energy flows.
articles.image_caption: Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodríguez during an official engagement
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Postpones Its Flagship Africa Summit Indefinitely. The Reason Is an Ebola Strain No Vaccine Can Stop.
articles.excerpt: The Fourth India-Africa Forum Summit, planned for New Delhi, was shelved after a Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in Congo reached 363 cases with no approved vaccine or treatment in sight.
articles.image_caption: Delegates at a previous India-Africa Forum Summit in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran's Oil Exports Have Collapsed to a Six-Year Low. India Cannot Afford to Wait for a Recovery.
articles.excerpt: Shipping data shows Iranian crude shipments fell to 209,000 barrels per day in May, down 89 percent from March, as the US blockade and Hormuz closure strangle Gulf energy flows.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker near the Strait of Hormuz, where shipping remains severely disrupted by the US-Iran conflict
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Tumbled 3% on the Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire. India Is Watching for the Hormuz Breakthrough That Has Not Come.
articles.excerpt: Brent fell to $95 as markets bet on a broader Iran deal. For India, the question is whether this ceasefire holds long enough to reopen the strait that carried 40 percent of its crude.
articles.image_caption: The Strait of Hormuz, a vital chokepoint for global oil supplies
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Chip Startups Are Heading to France. They Are Bringing Working Silicon, Not Slide Decks.
articles.excerpt: VerveSemi, AGNIT Semiconductors, and Netrasemi have been selected for Bharat Innovates 2026 in Nice. All three are at or near production.
articles.image_caption: A semiconductor chip wafer in production
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Are Quietly Shifting to Short-Term Indian Bonds. The Signal Is Hard to Ignore.
articles.excerpt: Two-thirds of top foreign bond purchases in March through May were in maturities under five years. The front end of the curve now offers better risk-adjusted carry — and the back end is a bet most fund managers do not want to take.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, where the MPC will announce its rate decision on Friday
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Trade Deal With Britain Is Stuck on Steel. Scotch Whisky Is Being Used as Leverage.
articles.excerpt: Britain's new steel safeguards cut tariff-free imports by 60 per cent. India is now reviewing the duty concessions it offered on whisky, automobiles and medical devices as a countermeasure.
articles.image_caption: UK Trade Minister Peter Kyle after returning from trade talks in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Just Proposed a 12.5% Tariff on India Over Forced Labour. Sixty Countries Are in the Crosshairs.
articles.excerpt: The Section 301 investigation is designed to rebuild the tariff architecture the Supreme Court dismantled in February. India rejected the allegations and said it would seek resolution through trade talks.
articles.image_caption: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced the proposed tariffs under Section 301
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rubio Told Congress That India Is Central to American Foreign Policy. He Was Not Exaggerating.
articles.excerpt: In a marathon Congressional testimony, the Secretary of State cited India more than any other partner — on trade, the Quad, de-escalation with Pakistan, and the Indo-Pacific strategy that now anchors Washington's Asia doctrine.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who cited India as central to American foreign policy during Congressional testimony
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's New Grid Rules Could Cut Solar Revenues by 11% and Wind by 48%. The Investors Are Already Walking.
articles.excerpt: KKR, Canada Pension Plan, Actis, and Macquarie-backed Blueleaf have warned Indian officials that tighter power grid penalties are advancing faster than the infrastructure to support them.
articles.image_caption: A solar energy installation in India, part of the country's push toward 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's New Trade Pact With Oman Bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. That May Matter More Than the Tariff Cuts.
articles.excerpt: The India-Oman CEPA grants duty-free access to 99% of Indian exports — but the agreement's real strategic value lies in Oman's coastline, which sits outside the world's most dangerous chokepoint.
articles.image_caption: The Port of Salalah in Oman, located outside the Strait of Hormuz on the Arabian Sea coastline
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Launched Its First Mass-Market Ethanol Motorcycles. The Price Difference Is Less Than a Tank of Petrol.
articles.excerpt: Hero MotoCorp's Splendor+ and HF Deluxe can now run on E85. With India importing 87% of its fossil fuel, the ₹172 premium on the cheapest model is a rounding error.
articles.image_caption: Hero MotoCorp's Splendor and HF Deluxe are India's best-selling motorcycle families
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Farmer's Daughter Died Because India's Biggest Medical Exam Was Cancelled. She Was Not the Last Victim.
articles.excerpt: Akanksha Chaturvedi scored well on NEET. Then the paper leak happened. The re-exam broke her. Now scammers are selling fake papers to desperate families for ₹20 lakh.
articles.image_caption: NEET aspirants face an uncertain future after the cancellation of the May 3 examination
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Just Agreed to Hand Over Its India Financials to the Antitrust Regulator. It Had Refused for Years.
articles.excerpt: The CCI found Apple abused its dominant position in 2024. Apple fought the case and withheld its books. A Delhi judge told the company to cooperate. Now it has.
articles.image_caption: Apple's iPhone market share in India has grown from 2 percent to 9 percent in five years
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Will Announce Its Rate Decision Tomorrow. It May Be the Hardest Call Sanjay Malhotra Has Ever Made.
articles.excerpt: With the rupee at record lows, crude oil near $96, and inflation still below target, India's central bank faces a policy dilemma that has no clean answer.
articles.image_caption: India's central bank faces a critical rate decision amid economic uncertainty
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is About to Place Its Largest-Ever Military Drone Order. The $2 Billion Will Go Entirely to Domestic Firms.
articles.excerpt: Lessons from the Pakistan confrontation and the Iran war have fast-tracked India's biggest unmanned systems purchase. Deliveries are expected within 18 to 24 months.
articles.image_caption: An Indian military unmanned aerial vehicle during a defence exercise
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Supreme Court Just Called Every Mobile Phone a 'Virtual Gambling House.' The Online Gaming Industry Is Reeling.
articles.excerpt: The court upheld state bans on online betting — even on games of skill — and backed 28% GST on the full value of bets. Dream11, MPL and 27 other companies face an existential reckoning.
articles.image_caption: The Supreme Court of India in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
